eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high pressure over Central Texas combined with southerly flow has maintained elevated humidity and suppressed vertical mixing, keeping daytime heating rates moderate and positioning Austin's maximum temperature near the upper 90s. Official National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance for August 14 projects highs of 98–100 °F under mostly sunny skies, consistent with climatological norms where mean daily maxima reach 96–98 °F this time of year. Trader consensus reflected in the 80 % implied probability for 96–97 °F incorporates these model outputs while accounting for possible afternoon cloud development or slight forecast revisions that could cap readings below 98 °F. Upcoming NWS afternoon updates and real-time observations from local stations will provide the final data for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current European model consensus and Météo-France guidance point to a maximum of 33–35 °C in Paris on 15 August, driven by increasing cloud cover and scattered afternoon thunderstorms that limit surface heating after a hotter mid-week period. The primary scientific factors are a weakening high-pressure ridge allowing modest Atlantic influence, reduced insolation, and localized convective cooling, which historically caps daily maxima 2–4 °C below clear-sky potential. Official forecasts cluster tightly around these values with typical ensemble spread of ±1–2 °C, while urban heat-island effects in central Paris could nudge readings toward the higher end of the range. Recent runs show stable steering patterns with no rapid warming signals, supporting trader emphasis on 34 °C as the modal outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA) place the daytime maximum in Taipei at 35–36 °C on August 15, with conditions described as clear to partly cloudy and afternoon occasional thundershowers.** This range directly explains why the two leading market outcomes sit at equal 40.5 % implied probability.

Key scientific drivers include the strength and timing of daytime heating under a warm, moist southwesterly flow typical of mid-August, the urban heat-island effect that can add 1–2 °C at the official station, and the counteracting influence of afternoon convection. Thundershowers can develop rapidly, increasing cloud cover and triggering evaporative cooling that caps the peak; a slight delay or reduction in shower activity allows readings to reach the higher end of the forecast. Model consensus and recent CWA heat alerts for northern Taiwan (possible 36–38 °C) support the narrow spread between 35 °C and 36 °C, while the modest 11 % chance assigned to 37 °C reflects the low probability of suppressed convection or stronger subsidence.

Upcoming CWA forecast updates and real-time observations on the 15th will determine which of the two leading outcomes resolves.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Beijing Capital International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Beijing Capital International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/beijing/ZBAA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble forecasts for Chengdu on August 15, 2026, converge on a daytime maximum near 36–37°C amid humid subtropical conditions typical of the Sichuan basin in mid-August. Afternoon thundershowers, modest variations in boundary-layer moisture, and local wind patterns create the primary uncertainty, with earlier or heavier precipitation likely capping the peak closer to 36°C while lighter or delayed activity allows brief clearing to push toward 37°C. Official guidance from sources such as timeanddate and BBC Weather aligns with this narrow range, and the closely matched market-implied probabilities on these two outcomes reflect traders’ assessment of the limited but meaningful spread in model solutions. Historical August baselines around 30–35°C provide context, though recent model runs show no strong signals for extremes outside 35–38°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from Malaysia’s Meteorological Department project a maximum of 34 °C for Kuala Lumpur on 15 August 2026 under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with no rain expected.** This aligns closely with the market’s heavy weighting toward 33 °C (51.5 %) and 34 °C (35.0 %), which together capture an 86.5 % implied probability.

Equatorial insolation in mid-August typically drives daytime maxima of 32–34 °C when surface heating is strong and humidity remains high (75–85 %), limiting evaporative cooling. Recent model runs show minimal day-to-day variability, with steering patterns and cloud cover not favoring significant suppression or enhancement of peak temperatures. Historical August records for the city cluster around 32–33 °C, so the slight market tilt toward 33 °C likely reflects residual uncertainty in exact measurement timing and any late-afternoon convective development.

No major tropical systems or abrupt shifts in regional circulation have appeared in the latest updates, keeping the 33–34 °C band as the consensus range. Traders are therefore pricing the narrow window between typical climatology and the official 34 °C guidance.

August climatology shows average daily highs of 38–40°C, with frequent exceedances of 40°C when sea-surface temperatures hover near 31°C and humidity remains elevated, limiting overnight cooling.

Saudi Arabia’s National Center for Meteorology has flagged above-normal temperatures (1–2°C warmer than average) across the Kingdom for summer 2026, including August, consistent with longer-term Red Sea coastal warming trends of roughly 0.45–1.2°C per decade. Recent observations confirm stable conditions with no significant cloud outbreaks, dust events, or wind shifts that would cap highs below 40°C. While individual forecasts can shift 1–2°C in the final 24–48 hours, the current consensus and elevated seasonal baseline keep the 40°C+ bin dominant at 72% implied probability, with lower bins reflecting only modest downside risk from any late revision.
